summary: @vertexa/prisma-fetch-engine impersonates @prisma/fetch-engine and executes a Rust binary from an unrelated personal GitHub fork
details: Package published under the @vertexa scope impersonates the official @prisma/fetch-engine: package.json declares author 'Tim Suchanek <suchanek@prisma.io>', homepage https://www.prisma.io, and repository github.com/prisma/prisma, and the README is copied verbatim from the legitimate package. The bundled getDownloadUrl (dist/chunk-CF6UJAP3.js) constructs a download URL rooted at https://github.com/lh0x00/prisma/releases/download/engines-b436f5b358bf3b9d72861631111333dd40434f73/ — a personal user's fork of Prisma, not the official prisma organization — pinned to a specific commit SHA under that fork's control. The package's download() path fetches this binary, chmod+x's it, and executes it as the Prisma query engine. Consumers transitively depending on this package resolve and run an attacker-controlled native binary on their build/host as part of Prisma's normal engine lifecycle, yielding remote code execution on the installer's machine. The publisher scope (@vertexa) does not match the publisher identity claimed in metadata (prisma.io), and the binary source host does not match the claimed publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
